section.title: Purpose
section.text: N-19 is where an LLM judges a diff. It is the semantic half of review: are the acceptance criteria evidenced, does the change fit the design anchor, is the breadcrumb at the fix site, is the ticket's one concern the only thing that changed. The mechanical half (the diff stays inside the declared files, no aggregate, lint, the suites) is code before the reviewer ever runs: N-16's close-out, N-23 to N-25's gate (rebuild/investigation/L13-llms-doing-scheduler-work.md#7-decisions-an-llm-makes-that-a-rule-could-make D21).

The reviewer is separate from the writer and shares no context with it (rebuild/investigation/02-MAPPING.md#2-validated-keep V15; the generator-verifier split works best with no shared context). It runs after the gate is green on the head sha, so it never re-runs tests (roles/reviewer.json breadcrumb WO-20261013-b6f3: a reviewer ran suites for 12 minutes on PR 145 for no new evidence). Its verdict is a record on the head sha that the merge (N-09) reads together with coq/gate; the owner holds the line through cards, never through the per-PR path (D15).

section.title: Input: the reviewer brief inside a seat run
section.text: The dispatch's target names pr and head_sha; the gate.verdict green for that head is the record that caused the dispatch. N-13 renders bundle_dir/brief.md with:
section.field: id and full title, concern, the design anchor text (the node volume section the ticket builds), the declared files, the acceptance commands with observed_exit_on_main (N-18) and expect_exit.

number, head sha, title, body (the worker's summary and evidence table from pr.opened), the diff (git diff base_sha..head_sha, rendered into the brief when under seats.json brief_diff_max_bytes, default 200 KB, else the reviewer reads it from the workspace).
the gate.verdict green record id and the gate page link (coq/gate-page status), with the suites that ran; informational, so the reviewer knows what was proved by code.

what to judge (section judgement); the output contract; "run nothing"; a changes verdict needs at least one observation with path, line, saw, expected; a passed verdict needs every criterion marked evidenced with the evidence line.
on a second review of the same ticket (a new head after review.changes), the prior review.changes record, so the reviewer checks that each observation was answered.
section.text: The workspace is read-only, detached at head_sha (N-14 base_ref refs/pull/<pr>/head, refused as head_moved if the ref no longer resolves to head_sha).

section.title: Output record: review.passed 201 or review.changes 422 on the head sha
section.text: The seat's structured output, review.result (record.schema.json#/$defs/review.result): verdict, head_sha as the reviewer saw it, criteria (one per acceptance id: evidenced with the evidence line, or the gap), observations (path, line, saw, expected; at least one for changes), design_fit, summary.

The node's record, committed by the close-out after the head check: review.passed, code 201 (record.schema.json#/$defs/review.passed), or review.changes, code 422 (#/$defs/review.changes). Both carry ticket, pr, head_sha, base_sha, run_id, dispatch_id (equal), attempt, lease (the reviewer seat lease, shared lease_ref, which N-09 requires and N-01 fences), gate_verdict_ref, criteria, observations, design_fit, summary and session_id. review.changes also carries shared failure_body: phase reviewer, outcome changes, failure_kind review.changes, so N-11 consumes it as it stands. ../N-09/record.schema.json#/$defs/review_passed is a subset of review.passed; every review.passed this node writes validates there (checked by the example below). Each criteria entry names the acceptance id it evidences, so through the ticket's acceptance[].proves it ticks a checklist item (nodes/N-31/spec.xml#views). The record is on the head sha: a new head gets a new review. A GitHub pull request review mirrors the verdict for the owner's reading; the store record is what the merge reads.

section.title: Mechanism: the brief, the run, the verdict committed by code
section.mermaid: flowchart LR G[gate.verdict green on head_sha] --> L[N-07 GrantDispatch phase reviewer] L --> B[N-13 brief; N-14 workspace detached at head_sha] B --> R[N-15 seat run, read-only] R --> S[seat.result done, run result_committed] S --> H{close-out: head check and output rules} H -- passed --> A[Commit review.passed 201, lease released, run closed_out] H -- changes --> C[Commit review.changes 422, lease released, run closed_out] H -- rejected --> X[phase.failed step head.check, output_rejected] A --> M[effect review.mirror to GitHub] C --> M
section.step: The run: the reviewer reads the brief, the diff and the changed files in the workspace; it runs no test, suite, lint, make target or podman command (denied by the fence: the gate already proved them); it returns review.result. N-15 commits seat.result done and the run reaches result_committed.

Close-out, function closeout(run) in scheduler/internal/closeout/reviewer.go, in the service as principal coq-svc acting as N-19, level-triggered on run entities in result_committed with a done reviewer seat.result. Head check: review.result.head_sha equals dispatch target head_sha, and the forge (credential forge-read) still reports that head for the pull request. Output rules: a changes verdict has at least one observation; a passed verdict has every criterion evidenced. A moved head is phase.failed step head.check with failure_kind head_moved (free, nothing charged, shared/contracts.xml#retry-owner); a failure of either output rule is phase.failed step head.check with failure_kind output_rejected and the reason (no_observations or open_criterion_on_pass); the same Commit releases the lease and moves the run to closed_out.

The verdict Commit, one Store.Do under operation key N-19/review.verdict/{pr}@{head_sha}@{run_id}/r1, fenced by the reviewer lease (shared/contracts.xml#fencing): the review.passed or review.changes record; Lease.Release of TICKET:reviewer:N; run:RUN_ID to closed_out with phase_record_ref the record id; an effects row in state intent for the mirror (provider github, action review.mirror). On review.passed the same Commit moves the ticket in_flight to pr_open so N-09 can merge it (a row shared/contracts.xml#ticket-transitions must add, owner N-19, trigger review.passed). On review.changes the ticket stays in_flight and N-11's attempt Commit moves it (row in_flight to retry_wait). A replay of the key returns the first reply; a stale token is 412 and nothing is written.

Mirror: after the Commit the outbox worker posts gh pr review --approve or --request-changes with the summary and observations, and advances the effect to done. A mirror that fails after its retries is phase.failed step review.mirror; it never undoes the record and never blocks the merge.
section.text: Model: roles/reviewer.json model.claude; argv only from ../../shared/seat-contract.xml#launch-flags; stall and wall clock by keys stall.seconds.reviewer and run.deadline_seconds.reviewer (../../shared/contracts.xml#timing); max turns and budget from seats.json reviewer.

section.title: What the reviewer judges and what code already checked

row.what: the diff stays inside the declared files; no aggregate; no runtime file
row.who: code: N-16 close-out before the push; N-25 gate pr-files

row.what: lint, the suites, the acceptance commands' exits
row.who: code: N-23 to N-25, coq/gate on the head sha

row.what: no em dash, UTC, contents element in long documents, no literal where config belongs
row.who: code: lint in the gate (lint/lint.sh rules carried into the suite)

row.what: every acceptance criterion is evidenced by the pull request body and the diff, not only claimed
the change does what the anchor says and nothing else; one concern
a breadcrumb comment sits at the fix site with what broke, why it mattered, why this fix, what it costs
row.who: the reviewer (presence is judgement; a lint can only find the word)

row.what: a regression guard still guards; a flipped acceptance flips for the right reason
row.who: the reviewer, reading observed_exit_on_main against the evidence

row.what: the design was not changed to fit the code (a ticket that edits a volume of this book to pass its own acceptance)
row.who: the reviewer, and the validator's anchor_moved on the next cut

row.what: an owner-surface change carries its screenshot proof
row.who: code checks the file exists (N-48); the reviewer judges that the picture shows the change

section.text: The reviewer never fixes the code (roles/reviewer.json forbidden, carried forward): an observation names path, line, saw, expected; the worker's next attempt answers it.

section.title: How it starts without an agent typing
section.text: gate.verdict green (N-08) on the pull request's head makes the ticket's reviewer phase desired: N-07 grants TICKET:reviewer:N by GrantDispatch (pr_open to in_flight); N-13 and N-14 prepare; N-15 runs. No one posts pr.opened to a reviewer, wakes a pane, or asks the architect. A review.changes reaches N-11, which charges the worker phase and re-enters N-07 through retry_wait.

section.title: Every wait, its timeout and its fallback

wait.fallback: N-12 kills a stalled run; N-15 commits the blocked seat.result; N-11 retries the review within the reviewer phase's attempts
phase.failed 500 step head.check reason forge_unreachable; no verdict is committed
phase.failed 500 step verdict.put; idempotent by the operation key
phase.failed 500 step review.mirror; the record stands and the merge proceeds

section.text: The reviewer waits for nothing: the gate was green before it started and the merge happens after it is gone.

section.title: Retries up to 3, then recover and report
section.text: A blocked review run (limits, stall, crash, no result) and a phase.failed output_rejected are retried by N-11 as a fresh reviewer run on the same head, charged to the reviewer phase (shared/contracts.xml#retry-owner); the rejection rides in the next brief. The close-out's own failures (head check unreachable, verdict put) are retried by the close-out in three passes, then phase.failed to N-11, charged once (row phase.failed). After the third charged failure the ticket is dead and N-28 posts one card (a reviewer on a stronger model by ruling, merge on the gate alone as an owner ruling for that head, or close).

A review.changes is not a retry of the review: it is the worker phase's attempt n+1, session resume-if-done (row review.changes). A review on a new head is a new grant with the prior review.changes attached.

section.title: Many agents at once
section.text: Many reviewers run at once, one per pull request head, each read-only in its own slot. A reviewer never resumes a worker's session and never shares a workspace with one (V15).

Collision 1, two reviewers for one head: GrantDispatch refuses a second reserved or running lease for the ticket and phase; a reviewer whose lease was revoked or expired has its verdict Commit refused 412 stale_token, so one head gets one verdict per live lease.

Collision 2, the head moves during the review (a worker push or N-09's update-branch): the head check refuses the stale review as head_moved; the new head's green gate leads to a new grant. No verdict is ever written on a head that is not the pull request's head.
Collision 3, the merge races the review: N-09 requires gate.verdict green and review.passed on the same head sha; a review.passed on an older head never merges a newer head.
Collision 4, two close-out passes for one run: both send the same operation key; the second replays the first reply.

Collision 5, the owner comments on the pull request: the reviewer reads only its brief; the owner holds through a card or the Controls hold; N-04's poll surfaces the comment as a record for the Alerts screen.

section.title: Status codes this node emits
section.code: Every criterion evidenced, on the head sha. Acts: N-09 merges when the gate is green on the same head.
At least one observation, on the head sha. Acts: N-11 charges the worker phase, attempt n+1.
step head.check (head_moved, free; output_rejected: no_observations, open_criterion_on_pass), verdict.put or review.mirror. Acts: N-11; a mirror-only failure never blocks the merge.
section.text: A blocked review run is N-15's seat.result 423, not this node's record.

section.title: State paths and the cleanup script for each

path.retention: freed when the run is closed_out

section.text: Review records live in the store on the head sha; the GitHub pull request review is a mirror. Nothing is written into the repository.

section.title: Permissions
section.text: The reviewer seat (fence from N-13, user coq-seat-NN): Read, Grep, Glob, Bash read-only (git diff|log|show|blame, rg, ls, cat); denied: Write, Edit, Agent, Task, make *, podman *, any test or lint command, gh of any kind, git push, git checkout|switch. The seat holds no forge credential and no store socket.

The close-out (coq-svc acting as N-19): Commits of review.passed, review.changes and phase.failed; Lease.Release of the reviewer lease; forge-read for the head check; the mirror's pull request review write through the outbox with a pull-requests-write credential (forge-pr names only N-16 today: shared/authority.xml#credential-matrix must add N-19 to its users).

section.title: Checklist with proof

item.proof: probe: a reviewer seat on a fixture pull request whose brief contains a trap line asking it to run make test ends with a permission denial naming make, and the verdict is still produced
go test ./internal/closeout -run TestReviewHeadMoved: a fake forge whose head differs from the dispatched head yields phase.failed step head.check reason head_moved and no review record

section.item: A stale review is never recorded on a moved head.

item.proof: go test TestChangesNeedObservations and TestPassNeedsAllCriteria: changes with zero observations and passed with an unevidenced criterion both yield phase.failed output_rejected

section.item: Kickback without evidence and approval with an open criterion are refused.

item.proof: go test TestVerdictCommit: one Store.Do writes the record, releases the lease, closes the run out and inserts the mirror effect; a replay of the key commits nothing new; a stale token is 412 with nothing written

section.item: The verdict, the release and the close-out are one Commit.

item.proof: check C22: the review.passed example validates against ../N-09/record.schema.json#/$defs/review_passed
check C22: the review.changes example validates against ../N-11/record.schema.json#/$defs/failure
go test TestMirrorFailureDoesNotBlock (N-09 fixture): a review.passed whose mirror effect failed still merges when the gate is green

section.item: The store is the truth; the GitHub review is a view.

item.proof: probe: the brief of a second review of a ticket contains the prior review.changes observations and the criteria entries reference them

section.item: A re-review checks that the prior observations were answered.

section.title: Monitoring
section.text: Counters: reviews_passed, reviews_changes, reviews_blocked_by_reason, review_seconds histogram, review_cost_usd, observations_per_changes histogram, head_moved_count, two_verdicts_defects. The Stats screen (N-40) shows the pass rate and the median time from gate green to review record; a median above seats.json review_latency_alert (default 900 s) is an alert on N-41 because a green pull request sitting unreviewed is the line's cost. The Machine screen (N-39) shows live reviews with pr, head and progress age.

section.title: Runbook
section.text: See a review: the record on the head sha in the store; the GitHub pull request review mirrors it; the transcript is in the run directory.

A dead review after 3 blocked runs: the card names the reasons; the options are a stronger model by ruling, merge on the gate alone (the owner's call, recorded as a ruling that N-09 reads for that head only), or close.
The owner disagrees with a review.passed: a hold from the Controls screen (N-42) stops the merge; a card records the ruling; the owner never edits a record.
Cleanup: run directories by cleanup-seat-runs.sh (N-15); slots by cleanup-workspaces.sh (N-14).

edge.record: seat.result done for a reviewer run (the brief ran inside the launcher's unit)
